```{r}

###########################################################
# PRAIM Screening Cohort Analysis (sample version)
# Data file: praim.csv  (from Dryad)
# Author: your name
###########################################################

## 0. Packages --------------------------------------------------------------

# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "broom")) # If needed
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)

## 1. Load data --------------------------------------------------------------

praim_raw <- read_csv("praim.csv")

cat("Rows in full data: ", nrow(praim_raw), "\n")

## 2. Build main variables ---------------------------------------------------

praim <- praim_raw %>%
  mutate(
    # exposure: use of AI
    ai_used = ifelse(used_ai_viewer, 1L, 0L),
    ai_group = factor(ai_used, levels = c(0, 1),
                      labels = c("No AI", "AI-assisted")),

    # outcome: cancer
    cancer = ifelse(cancer_detected, 1L, 0L),

    # recall indicator
    recall = ifelse(had_recall, 1L, 0L)
  )

cat("Finished building key variables.\n")

## 3. Take a random sample for analysis --------------------------------------

set.seed(123)  # for reproducibility
praim_small <- praim %>% sample_frac(0.05)

cat("Rows in sampled data: ", nrow(praim_small), "\n")

## 后面所有分析都用 praim_small，而不是 praim

cat("\n----- Summary of sampled data -----\n")
print(summary(praim_small[, c("ai_group", "cancer", "recall")]))

## 4. Descriptive statistics -------------------------------------------------

desc_tbl <- praim_small %>%
  group_by(ai_group) %>%
  summarise(
    n_screened  = n(),
    cancer_n    = sum(cancer == 1),
    cancer_prop = cancer_n / n_screened,
    recall_n    = sum(recall == 1),
    recall_prop = recall_n / n_screened,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("\n----- Descriptive table (Cancer & Recall by AI group, SAMPLE) -----\n")
print(desc_tbl)

## 5. Screening performance measures ----------------------------------------

perf <- praim_small %>%
  group_by(ai_group) %>%
  summarise(
    n_screened = n(),
    cancers    = sum(cancer),
    recalls    = sum(recall),
    detection_rate_per_1000 = cancers / n_screened * 1000,
    recall_rate_per_1000    = recalls / n_screened * 1000,
    ppv_recall = ifelse(recalls > 0, cancers / recalls, NA_real_),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("\n----- Screening performance by AI group (SAMPLE) -----\n")
print(perf)

## 6. Logistic regression ----------------------------------------------------

# 6.1 Crude model
fit_crude <- glm(cancer ~ ai_group,
                 data = praim_small,
                 family = binomial())

cat("\n----- Crude logistic regression (SAMPLE): cancer ~ ai_group -----\n")
print(summary(fit_crude))

cat("\nOdds ratios (crude model, SAMPLE):\n")
print(exp(cbind(OR = coef(fit_crude),
                confint.default(fit_crude))))

# 6.2 Adjusted model (control for reader_set)
fit_adj <- glm(cancer ~ ai_group + reader_set,
               data = praim_small,
               family = binomial())

cat("\n----- Adjusted logistic regression (SAMPLE): cancer ~ ai_group + reader_set -----\n")
print(summary(fit_adj))

cat("\nOdds ratios (adjusted model, SAMPLE):\n")
print(exp(cbind(OR = coef(fit_adj),
                confint.default(fit_adj))))

## 7. Plot detection & recall rates -----------------------------------------

perf_long <- perf %>%
  select(ai_group, detection_rate_per_1000, recall_rate_per_1000) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(detection_rate_per_1000, recall_rate_per_1000),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(metric = recode(
    metric,
    detection_rate_per_1000 = "Cancer detection rate (per 1000)",
    recall_rate_per_1000    = "Recall rate (per 1000)"
  ))

p <- ggplot(perf_long, aes(x = ai_group, y = value, fill = ai_group)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Rate per 1000 women",
    title = "Screening performance by AI use (Sample)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

cat("\nPlot created from SAMPLE data. Use print(p) to view in RStudio.\n")
print(p)

## 8. Save outputs -----------------------------------------------------------

write_csv(perf, "praim_performance_by_ai_group_sample.csv")

capture.output(summary(fit_crude),
               file = "model_crude_summary_sample.txt")
capture.output(summary(fit_adj),
               file = "model_adjusted_summary_sample.txt")

cat("\nSample-based analysis completed.\n")


```
